Enstone Primary School
Exceptional Absence Requests
Exceptional Absence Requests
Regular school attendance is of the utmost importance for your child. Family holidays and days out should be taken during the 13 weeks of school holiday, not during term time.
Attendance below 95% is regarded as “Persistent Absenteeism” and the DfE collect data from all schools to monitor pupils’ attendance and identify those whose education and wellbeing is being impacted in this way.
95% attendance = the equivalent of missing half a day’s schooling per fortnight.
90% attendance = the equivalent of missing half a day's schooling per week.
80% attendance = the equivalent of missing a whole day's schooling per week.
If there is a reason that you need to take your child out of school during teaching time, please complete an Exceptional Absence Request form and return this to school well in advance of the proposed absence. In some cases, we may be able to authorise the absence. In all cases, we need to be able to account for your child's whereabouts, if they are not in school.
Thank you for helping us to keep your child safe and helping to ensure their learning is not disrupted.
Exceptional Absence Request Form

Enstone Primary School
French
The aims of Primary Language teaching at Enstone Primary School are to enable all children to:
French is taught from Year 3 upwards, as the key language of our Primary Languages curriculum. Prior to this, children will be exposed to "language tasters" such as learning to say hello/goodbye, or learning to count in a variety of different languages.
Where possible, we bring children's own language experiences into the classroom, whether this be languages spoken at home or phrases and vocabulary they have learned on trips abroad.
In Year 4, our pupils attend the Modern Foreign Languages Festival at Chipping Norton School, where they are supported by Key Stage 3 students as they learn some new vocabulary in French, Spanish, Italian and German.
Our curriculum plans, based on units from the Twinkl French Scheme, cover topics such as meeting and greeting, hobbies, families and friends, travel and shopping. French speaking is also brought into our classrooms through some of our instructional language (sit down, line up), through taking the registers or ordering meals, and through making requests or asking questions (may I go to the toilet, what is the time?). This helps to keep some of the key vocabulary fresh in our pupils' minds, as well as building confidence in the spoken word.

pageCache.pageTitle: Enstone Primary School - History and Geography
pageCache.text:
Enstone Primary School
History and Geography
History and Geography
Our Geography and History lessons are delivered using Kapow schemes of work. In both subject areas, a creative, investigative approach encourages children to explore, discuss, reason, draw comparisons and understand how our world today has been shaped, as well as thinking about how the choices we make now might affect the planet as we journey further into the 21st century.
We are a Green Flag “Eco School” and our work on the environment and sustainability is woven through our whole curriculum.
We use a range of sources of information, such as maps, aerial photographs and atlases in geography, and a broad selection of primary and secondary sources in history. We often link our class trips, visits and workshops to our history and geography topics, for example visiting areas of geographical interest, to acquire the skills of interpretation and enquiry, or visiting museums and historic sites to provide a more immersive experience of each historical period studied.
We are fortunate enough to have fantastic school grounds, which means we can take much of our learning outdoors, either on our own site or slightly further afield into the Ditchley Estate, or Heythrop Park Estate, both of which kindly support us by allowing us to use areas of their grounds and access suitable spots for field study.

pageCache.text:
Enstone Primary School
PSHE and RSE
PSHE and RSE
At Enstone Primary School we nurture our children as unique individuals in a safe and secure environment, to ensure they thrive and fulfil their potential.
The importance of PSHE/RSE
Our personal, social and health education (PSHE) programme alongside our relationships, sex and health education (RSE) programme promote children’s personal, social and economic development, as well as their health and wellbeing. These help to give children the knowledge and understanding they need to lead confident, healthy and independent lives and to become informed, responsible citizens. We believe it is the duty of our school to give our young people the learning that will enable them to live safe, fulfilled and healthy lives. This includes giving them all the skills they will need to survive in the modern world. Our PSHE and RSE Policy covers our school’s approach and attitude towards PSHE and RSE, and outlines key content which is taught at each key stage. It is available below in the documents section.
At Enstone Primary School, children’s wellbeing, happiness and safety are our first priority, and PSHE is the key vehicle through which we share this with children. We regard PSHE as an important, integral component of the whole curriculum, central to our approach and at the core of our ethos. In accordance with government guidance, the PSHE and RSE curriculum focus on developing personal attributes including love, courage, truth and respect.
As part of our PSHE curriculum, we include RSE, making sure all our children are prepared for the changes which will happen to their bodies, along with how to deal with transitions in their lives.
Our curriculum is broad and balanced, ensuring it:
The curriculum is planned in accordance with all relevant government guidance as referenced in Appendix 7 of the PSHE and RSE Policy document. It meets the learning objectives as set out in the Relationships and Sex Education and Health Education (England) Regulations 2019.
Organisation/Provision
PSHE is delivered within a whole school approach which includes:
The curriculum is delivered by all staff and is supplemented by visitors and other external agencies to give children the highest quality provision available. However, we do not allow external agencies to take over this provision as it is important that PSHE and RSHE are seen as things we can talk about at school. Furthermore, class teachers know their children and will be best placed to support additional needs, or scaffold difficult and sensitive topics which make a child feel vulnerable.
At school, we use Jigsaw, a health and wellbeing whole school approach scheme. This is supplemented, when appropriate, with up to date resources for more difficult issues e.g. bullying, racism, homophobia etc. Along with the scheme, we also ensure that we incorporate and respect all social, moral, spiritual and cultural issues, encouraging our children to think about their place within Britain as citizens. We include the five British Values (democracy, rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of different faiths/beliefs) within our teaching to establish an effective and safe school environment.
The Jigsaw Scheme provides structured lessons for each year group. The scheme is adapted by teachers to suit their class needs and to ensure age appropriateness. The scheme is progressive throughout the school, showing the development in knowledge from Reception to Year 6. It also meets the needs set out in the RSHE government guidance. More information is included in the policy document, available in the section below.

Enstone Primary School
Wrap Around Care
Wrap Around Care
Extended hours provision - 8:00am - 5:15pm
Normal school operating hours are from 8:40am - 3:15pm. Class 1 pupils are dropped off at the side door to the hall. Children in Classes 2, 3 and 4 are dropped off on the main playground.
Early Birds Club runs from 8:00am each morning. Sessions must be pre-booked. Parents may drop their children off between 8:00am and 8:10am, and they will be cared for in the club, accessing a range of toys and activities, until the start of the school day. Breakfast is not provided - children should eat before they arrive. Early Birds Club costs £4.50 per session and may be booked termly in advance (recommended to secure your place) or on an ad hoc basis weekly (space permitting). A booking form for Early Birds Club may be found below. Payments for this club can only be made by cash or cheque.
After school sports/arts clubs run from 3:15pm to 4:15pm daily and vary from term to term. We work with several external partners, as well as running some clubs in-house. After school clubs run by the school are charged at £4.50 per session. Costs for external club providers may differ. Booking information is sent out towards the end of each term, for parents to book ahead for the next term. Bookings are made and paid for via Parent Pay, or using the direct website booking systems of our sports partners.
Currently, we are working with the following sports partners:
In-house we currently offer:
If your child qualifies for the Pupil Premium Grant, you may be able to access free or subsidised provision in Early Birds or After School Clubs (but not the after school extended hours care).
Please enquire at the school office for more information.
After school care runs from the end of the school day (3:15pm) until 5:15pm and is run as two concurrent sessions, with the option to book for just the early session, the late session following a sports/arts club, or both childcare sessions. The after school care clubs are called Busy Bees and Chill Zone.
Busy Bees Club and Chill Zone are run by Mrs Lisa Thompson, our after school club leader. The first session (Busy Bees) is a multi-activity club, with a mixture of structured and unstructured play opportunities. These vary according to the weather, the time of year, and the interests and ages of the children. The cost of this club is £4 per session. The second session (Chill Zone) takes the tempo down a little, with some quieter activities, for example stories, colouring, puzzles and board games. The cost of this club is £5 per session. Food is not provided, but children attending the later session (Chill Zone) are encouraged to bring a suitable healthy snack from home that will be eaten at the start of the session.
Children may attend:
Please be very clear, when booking, which sessions you require. If children have been to a sports/arts club on school premises, and are going on to attend Chill Zone, their club leader will ensure they are delivered to the right place.,
Please note that all bookings, whether weekly or termly, must be paid for in advance. Once booked, sessions are non-refundable and non-transferable.

Enstone Primary School
Enrichment
Music
Music
Music
Music plays a very important part in the life of the school. Many children in Key Stage 2 learn to play the recorder and from Year 3 onwards, pupils may choose to learn a woodwind or brass instrument with the Music for Schools Foundation or guitar/ukulele with "Create Music". There is a popular Key Stage 2 school choir and the whole school regularly take part in festivals, concerts and productions.
Every year, we take our Year 4, 5 and 6 pupils to Chipping Norton Music Festival, to participate in a schools' workshop and concert. In 2025, we were delighted to join other schools in the Chipping Norton Town Hall to learn and perform a varied repertoire of songs old and new, including a beautiful set of songs about the origins of the dreamcatcher.
Our pupils also have opportunities to attend workshops and concerts organised by the County Music Service. On one occasion, the KS1 children were lucky enough to be joined by author Julia Donaldson and her husband for a morning of singing based on her popular picture books. In previous years children in years 5 and 6 have been to the Royal Albert Hall as part of the ‘Oxfordshire Massed Choir’. Being accompanied by the Oxfordshire Youth Orchestra plus a chamber choir, and singing on stage in the Royal Albert Hall really is a musical experience second-to-none. Every year the school holds a "Musical Extravaganza" showcase assembly where any children who learn musical instruments or have professional vocal coaching are invited to perform to an audience of friends and parents. This year we enjoyed performances from the school choir, recorder groups and many individual performers aged from 7 to 11 years.
We are proud to celebrate the musical achievements of our pupils and were delighted to be awarded Music Mark, in recognition of our commitment to musical education. In our July 2022 Ofsted report, inspectors commented:
"Music is the beating heart of Enstone."

Enstone Primary School
Music
Music
"Music is the beating heart of Enstone." Ofsted 2022
We deliver a Music curriculum based on the "Charanga" English Model Music Curriculum Scheme.
Charanga’s English Model Music Curriculum Scheme is aligned with the National Curriculum for Music and the non-statutory Model Music Curriculum (MMC) Guidance published by the DfE in 2021. The scheme follows a spiral approach to musical learning, with children revisiting, building and extending their knowledge and skills incrementally. This means that their learning is consolidated and built upon, increasing confidence.
When creating our long term planning cycles, we choose units from the scheme to ensure a breadth and balance of musical genres and styles are taught in each year group.
If you follow the link to the Music page on our Enrichment tab, you will be able to find out more about our extra curricular provision and opportunities for tuition and performance.

P.E. and School Sport
P.E. and School Sport
PE and School Sport play an important part in the life of the school. Pupils participate in a minimum of 2 hours curriculum PE each week and also have daily opportunities to be active during playtimes and other lessons. There are many extra-curricular sports clubs and the Chipping Norton School Sports Partnership run a variety of workshops and inter-school competitions throughout the academic year.
In academic year 2024-25 we achieved our GOLD SPORTS MARK for the seventh year running. This award recognises the many different activities and opportunities which are on offer to our pupils every year.
